name: Cyber Resilience Act
description: Controls and evidence for the manufacturer obligations of the EU Cyber Resilience Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/2847): essential requirements (Annex I, Parts I and II), obligations of manufacturers (Art. 13), reporting (Art. 14) and documentation and conformity (Annexes V, VII, VIII). DRAFT: the mapping has not been reviewed against the regulation yet.

categories.name: Product security requirements (Annex I, Part I)

controls.name: Appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks
controls.description: The product is designed, developed and produced so that it ensures an appropriate level of cybersecurity based on the risks (Annex I, Part I, (1); Art. 13).

controls.name: Cybersecurity risk assessment
controls.description: A cybersecurity risk assessment of the product exists and is taken into account in planning, design, development, production, delivery and maintenance.

controls.name: Risk assessment is kept up to date
controls.description: The risk assessment is reviewed and updated during the support period, in particular after relevant vulnerabilities and changes.

controls.name: No known exploitable vulnerabilities
controls.description: The product is made available on the market without known exploitable vulnerabilities (Annex I, Part I, (2)(a)).
Regular vulnerability scanning must be performed
controls.name: Vulnerability Scanning
Known vulnerabilities by severity
controls.description: The number of known vulnerabilities of the product stays within the accepted limits per severity.

controls.name: Secure by default configuration
controls.description: The product is made available with a secure by default configuration, including the possibility to reset it to its original state (Annex I, Part I, (2)(b)).
Secure configuration must be enforced by default
controls.name: Secure Default Configuration
Reset to original state
controls.description: The product can be reset to its original, secure state.

controls.name: No default or shared credentials
controls.description: The product does not ship with default or shared credentials; credentials are unique per device or are set at first use.

controls.name: Security updates
controls.description: Vulnerabilities can be addressed through security updates, including automatic updates by default with a clear opt-out and notification of available updates (Annex I, Part I, (2)(c)).
Automatic updates must check for updates within appropriate intervals
controls.name: Update Check Interval

controls.description: Automatic updates must be enabled by default
controls.name: Automatic Updates by Default

controls.description: Users must be able to postpone updates and receive notifications
controls.name: User Update Control
Protection from unauthorized access
controls.description: The product ensures protection from unauthorized access through appropriate control mechanisms (authentication, identity or access management) and reports possible unauthorized access (Annex I, Part I, (2)(d)).
Access control mechanisms must be implemented at critical points
controls.name: Access Control Mechanisms

controls.description: Password policies must be enabled for identity management
controls.name: Password Policies

controls.description: Unauthorized access attempts must be reported
controls.name: Unauthorized Access Reporting

controls.description: Multi-factor authentication must be enabled for administrative access
controls.name: Multi-Factor Authentication

controls.description: Anomaly detection mechanisms must be enabled
controls.name: Anomaly Detection
Debug and service interfaces are protected
controls.description: Debug, service and manufacturing interfaces are disabled, locked or protected by authentication in the delivered product.

controls.name: Confidentiality of data
controls.description: The confidentiality of stored, transmitted and otherwise processed data is protected, for example by encryption of data at rest and in transit with state of the art mechanisms (Annex I, Part I, (2)(e)).
Data at rest must be encrypted
controls.name: Encryption at Rest

controls.description: Strong cryptographic algorithms must be used
controls.name: Cryptographic Algorithm Strength

controls.description: Data in transit must be encrypted
controls.name: Encryption in Transit
Cryptographic keys are stored protected
controls.description: Keys and secrets are stored in protected storage (for example secure element, key store) and not in clear text in the product or its firmware image.

controls.name: Integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration
controls.description: The integrity of data, commands, programs and configuration is protected against unauthorized manipulation, and corruption is reported (Annex I, Part I, (2)(f)).
Secure protocols must be enabled for data transmission
controls.name: Secure Transmission Protocols
Integrity of software and firmware
controls.description: Software and firmware are protected against unauthorized modification, for example by signed updates, secure boot and verified update packages.

controls.name: Source integrity
controls.description: Changes to the source code are traceable and protected: commits are signed and changes are reviewed.

controls.name: Data minimisation
controls.description: Only data that is adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the intended use is processed (Annex I, Part I, (2)(g)).
Data minimization techniques must be enabled
controls.name: Data Minimization

controls.description: Automated deletion of data must be configured
controls.name: Automated Data Deletion
Availability of essential functions
controls.description: The availability of essential and basic functions is protected, also after an incident, including resilience and mitigation measures against denial of service attacks (Annex I, Part I, (2)(h)).
DDoS protection mechanisms must be activated
controls.name: DDoS Protection

controls.description: Backup mechanisms must be enabled for critical data flows
controls.name: Backup of critical data
Essential functions stay available
controls.description: Essential and basic functions remain available after an incident, including resilience against denial of service.

controls.name: Minimise negative impact on other services
controls.description: The product minimises its own negative impact on the availability of services provided by other devices or networks (Annex I, Part I, (2)(i)).
Standard protocols must be listed and only required interfaces enabled
controls.name: Interface and Protocol Inventory
Limited attack surfaces
controls.description: The product is designed, developed and produced to limit attack surfaces, including external interfaces (Annex I, Part I, (2)(j)).
Risk assessment must be mapped to services and controls
controls.name: Risk Assessment Mapping

controls.description: Only required interfaces and protocols must be enabled
controls.name: Minimal Attack Surface
Reduce the impact of incidents
controls.description: The product reduces the impact of an incident using appropriate exploitation mitigation mechanisms and techniques (Annex I, Part I, (2)(k)).

controls.name: Exploitation mitigations are applied
controls.description: Hardening and exploitation mitigations are applied, for example memory protection, compiler hardening flags, sandboxing and least privilege.

controls.name: Security logging and monitoring
controls.description: Security related information is provided by recording and monitoring relevant internal activity, with an opt-out for the user (Annex I, Part I, (2)(l)).
Activity logging must be enabled for security-relevant activities
controls.name: Security Activity Logging

controls.description: Identity activity must be tracked and available
controls.name: Identity Activity Tracking

controls.description: Logging opt-out mechanism must be available to users
controls.name: Logging Opt-Out

controls.description: Security data must be available to users
controls.name: Security Data Access
Secure removal and transfer of data
controls.description: Users can securely and easily remove all data and settings permanently and, where data can be transferred to other products, this happens securely (Annex I, Part I, (2)(m)).
Secure data deletion mechanism must be activated
controls.name: Secure Data Deletion
Secure transfer of data
controls.description: Where data can be transferred to other products or systems, the transfer is secure.

categories.name: Vulnerability handling requirements (Annex I, Part II)

controls.name: Identify components and vulnerabilities, software bill of materials
controls.description: Vulnerabilities and components are identified and documented, including a software bill of materials in a commonly used and machine-readable format covering at least the top-level dependencies (Annex I, Part II, (1)).

controls.name: SBOM exists for every release
controls.description: A software bill of materials in a commonly used, machine-readable format exists for each release.

controls.name: SBOM is complete and valid
controls.description: The SBOM covers at least the top-level dependencies and is valid in its format.

controls.name: Remediate vulnerabilities without delay
controls.description: Vulnerabilities are addressed and remediated without delay, including by providing security updates; security updates are provided separately from functionality updates where technically feasible (Annex I, Part II, (2); Art. 13).

controls.name: Remediation within the defined time
controls.description: Known vulnerabilities are triaged and fixed within the defined service levels.

controls.name: Security updates are separable
controls.description: Security updates can be installed separately from functionality updates where technically feasible.

controls.name: Regular tests and reviews
controls.description: Effective and regular tests and reviews of the security of the product are applied (Annex I, Part II, (3)).

controls.name: Security testing in the development process
controls.description: Security tests (static analysis, dependency scanning, tests) run regularly and on every release.

controls.name: Code review
controls.description: Changes are reviewed by a second person before they are merged.

controls.name: Public disclosure of fixed vulnerabilities
controls.description: Once a security update is available, information about fixed vulnerabilities is publicly disclosed, including description, affected products, impact, severity and remediation guidance (Annex I, Part II, (4)).

controls.name: Fixed vulnerabilities are disclosed
controls.description: An advisory exists for every fixed vulnerability.

controls.name: Advisories are valid CSAF documents
controls.description: Published advisories are valid CSAF documents that are provided over an encrypted transport.

controls.name: Coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy
controls.description: A policy on coordinated vulnerability disclosure is put in place and enforced (Annex I, Part II, (5)).

controls.name: Disclosure policy is published
controls.description: A coordinated vulnerability disclosure policy is published and describes how vulnerabilities can be reported and handled.

controls.name: Sharing information about vulnerabilities
controls.description: Measures are taken to facilitate the sharing of information about potential vulnerabilities, including a contact address for reporting (Annex I, Part II, (6)).

controls.name: Reporting contact is provided
controls.description: A contact address or channel for reporting vulnerabilities is provided and monitored.

controls.name: Secure distribution of updates
controls.description: Mechanisms for the secure distribution of updates are provided to ensure that vulnerabilities are fixed or mitigated in a timely manner (Annex I, Part II, (7)).

controls.name: Updates are distributed securely
controls.description: Updates are signed and distributed over an authenticated channel; their authenticity is verified before installation.

controls.name: Security patches without delay and free of charge
controls.description: Security patches are disseminated without delay and, unless agreed otherwise for tailor-made products, free of charge, together with advisory messages (Annex I, Part II, (8)).

controls.name: Patches are provided without delay
controls.description: Security patches are made available without delay after a fix exists.

controls.name: Patches are free of charge
controls.description: Security patches are provided free of charge, with advisory messages on the action to take.

controls.name: Due diligence for third-party components
controls.description: Due diligence is exercised when integrating components from third parties, including open source components, so that they do not compromise the cybersecurity of the product; vulnerabilities in components are reported to their maintainers (Art. 13).

controls.name: Component due diligence
controls.description: Third-party components are selected and monitored with regard to their security and support status.

controls.name: Support period
controls.description: The support period reflects the time the product is expected to be in use and is at least five years, unless the product is expected to be used for less; it is clearly stated (Art. 13).

controls.name: Support period is determined
controls.description: A support period is determined and justified.

controls.name: Support period is communicated
controls.description: The end of the support period is communicated to users.

controls.name: User information and instructions
controls.description: The product is accompanied by the information and instructions to the user required by Annex II, including the contact point for vulnerability reports and secure use (Art. 13; Annex II).

controls.name: User information is provided
controls.description: The user information and instructions required by Annex II are provided.

controls.name: Documentation is retained
controls.description: The technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity are kept available for at least ten years after the product has been placed on the market or for the support period, whichever is longer (Art. 13).

controls.name: Retention of documentation
controls.description: Technical documentation and declaration of conformity are retained for the required time.

categories.name: Reporting obligations (Art. 14)
categories.description: Reporting of actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents

controls.name: Reporting process
controls.description: A process exists to report actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents: early warning without undue delay and within 24 hours of becoming aware, a notification within 72 hours and a final report (Art. 14).

controls.name: Reporting process is defined
controls.description: The reporting process, responsibilities and templates are defined and tested.

controls.name: Exploited vulnerabilities are reported in time
controls.description: Actively exploited vulnerabilities were reported within the required time limits.

controls.name: Severe incidents are reported in time
controls.description: Severe incidents with an impact on the security of the product were reported within the required time limits.

controls.name: Users are informed
controls.description: Users are informed about actively exploited vulnerabilities and severe incidents and about the measures they can take.

categories.name: Documentation and conformity
categories.description: Technical documentation, declaration of conformity and conformity assessment

controls.name: Product class and conformity route
controls.description: The product class (default, important class I or II, critical; Annexes III and IV) is determined and the matching conformity assessment procedure (Annex VIII) is chosen (Arts. 7, 8, 32).

controls.name: Product class is determined
controls.description: The product class is determined and documented.

controls.name: Conformity assessment procedure is chosen
controls.description: The conformity assessment procedure that matches the class is chosen and carried out.

controls.name: Technical documentation
controls.description: The technical documentation according to Annex VII is complete and up to date (Art. 31, Annex VII).

controls.name: Technical documentation is complete
controls.description: The technical documentation contains the elements required by Annex VII.

controls.name: EU declaration of conformity
controls.description: An EU declaration of conformity according to Annex V is drawn up and the CE marking is affixed (Arts. 28, 29).

controls.name: Declaration of conformity is issued
controls.description: An EU declaration of conformity exists for the released version.

controls.name: CE marking is affixed
controls.description: The CE marking is affixed visibly to the product or its documentation.

controls.name: Product identification
controls.description: The product can be identified (type, batch or version) and the manufacturer and contact point are stated (Art. 13).

controls.name: Product and manufacturer are identified
controls.description: Type, version or batch and manufacturer information are provided.
